item.title: UT Austin's new 3D printer tech creates bodies that feel real
item.description: Researchers at The University of Texas at Austin have developed a new 3D‑printing method that uses nothing but light and a single, inexpensive resin to create lifelike anatomical models with bone‑hard cores and soft, tissue‑like exteriors. Born from a serendipitous discovery at Sandia National Laboratories, the technique — called CRAFT — could give medical schools a realistic, low‑cost alternative to cadavers while opening the door to new designs in protective gear and advanced materials.

item.title: Metrics suggest Texas' offense is one of the best in the country. Does Sean Miller believe that?
item.description: The Longhorns face Louisiana State on Tuesday at Moody Center with a chance to make it five straight wins, and they're entrenched in the middle of the Southeastern Conference with Texas A&M and Missouri at 7-5. The Tigers are 2-10 in SEC play so far, but they're a dangerous team. Head coach Sean Miller said they can't overlook them.

item.title: Which national teams have never won a medal in the Winter Olympics?
item.description: Of the 122 current National Olympic Committees (NOCs) that have ever sent athletes to the Winter Olympic Games, 92 are competing in Milan Cortina. The bid to win a medal is more elusive for some than others.

item.title: Investigators retesting evidence, confirming alibis in 1999 murder of Rockdale teenager Sonya Wallace
item.description: This week marks 27 years since a teenager disappeared from Rockdale, only for investigators to find her body roughly 30 miles away, nearly a month later. Now, detectives are taking another look at the case with the help of advancements in DNA technology.
